taxonomy:
Below is a pragmatic taxonomy by primary solving objective/mechanics. Each category has brief notes and is populated with your games.

A) Draw a path/loop (no branching)
- Closed single-loop (edge or cell-center)
  - Slitherlink: Loop on edges so each numbered cell has that many incident loop-edges.
  - Masyu: Loop through circles; black = turn with straight before/after, white = straight through with turn next to it.
  - Moon-or-Sun: Masyu-like with “moon/sun” symbols and added adjacency/ordering rules.
  - Dotchi-Loop: Loop obeys “either-or” clue choices per cell.
  - Mid-loop: Loop constrained by midpoint/adjacency counts around cells.
  - Suraromu (Slalom): Loop threads through “gates” in specified ways.
- Loop with auxiliary shading/marking
  - Yajilin: Draw a single loop while blackening cells; arrows give counts of black cells in their direction.
- Open single path / snake
  - Hebi: Draw a single non-branching “snake” path satisfying head/tail/turn/length-style clues (snake does not close).
- Pair-connection paths
  - Numberlink: Connect matching numbers with non-crossing paths (often with full coverage or given coverage rules).
- Line networks with shape/length constraints
  - Sashigane: From numbered “angle” cells, extend two orthogonal arms; arm lengths satisfy the clue and obey non-overlap rules.
  - Juosan: Connect numbers with straight segments so segment sums/equalities match targets (sum/equation-based line network).
  - Nagareru: Route directed “flows” along arrows/straight paths so counts or exits match given constraints.

B) Partition/tiling of the grid into regions (polyomino/rectangles/tiles)
- Rectangular partition by area
  - Shikaku: Partition into rectangles; each number is the area of its rectangle.
- Polyomino partition by local size constraints
  - Fillomino: Partition into polyominoes whose sizes equal their internal numbers; same-sized regions may not touch orthogonally.
  - Evolomino: Fillomino-variant where touching regions’ sizes must differ by exactly 1.
  - Five Cells: Partition the grid into 5-cell polyominoes (pentomino-sized regions).
- Room-by-room specified shapes/tiles
  - LITS: In each outlined room, place exactly one tetromino of type L/I/T/S; identical shapes may not touch orthogonally across rooms and 2×2 of filled is forbidden.
  - Shakashaka: Place right-triangle halves in white squares so the remaining unfilled white space forms only rectangles.
- Pair/twin-region tilings
  - Double Choco: Partition the whole grid into region-pairs that are congruent (two identical shapes per pair), following room/color constraints.
  - Choco Banana: Twin/pair tiling with two “flavors” (two-color congruent-region pairing variant).
- Packing from item lists (sizes given; fit items into an area)
  - Yosenabe: Pack given “ingredients” (areas/sizes) into a pot region without overlap; positions/sizes often clued.
  - Tilepaint: Tile-based painting; place given tiles/shaded cells to meet row/column/region quotas (paint-by-tiles variant).

C) Cell shading/painting (binary: black/white) with structural/visibility rules
- Islands-and-sea family
  - Nurikabe: Black “sea” is one connected region with no 2×2 black; each number is a white “island” of that size; islands separated.
  - Nuritwin: Nurikabe variant with “twin” island constraints (e.g., islands paired by equal size/shape).
- Visibility / sight-line counts and local sums
  - Kurodoko: Place blacks so each numbered white cell “sees” exactly that many white cells in the four orthogonal directions; white area is connected; no adjacent black cells.
  - Kurotto: Shade cells; each circled number gives the total of shaded cells in its contiguous white region around it (sum-in-region style).
- Room/run-length and local placement rules
  - Heyawake: Shade to satisfy per-room black counts; white paths cannot run straight through more than a limited number of rooms; no 2×2 blacks; white area connected.
  - Norinori: In every room, shade exactly two orth-adjacent cells (a domino); shaded cells from different rooms cannot touch orthogonally.
  - Hitori: Shade duplicates so numbers left white are unique in each row/column; no orth-adjacent blacks; white area connected.
- Illumination/coverage
  - Akari (Light Up): Place bulbs to light all white cells; bulbs see along rows/columns; numbered blocks limit adjacent bulbs; bulbs cannot see each other.
- Maze-style shading and “capes”
  - Nurimeizu: Shade to form a proper maze consistent with given straight/turn/branching counts or entrance/exit constraints.
  - Nurimisaki: Shade so each numbered “cape” cell has a straight white protrusion of that length ending against black/border; standard connectivity/2×2 rules apply.
- Liar variants (some clues deliberately false)
  - Usowan: A liar variant (base may be sight-line/loop/etc.); determine which clues lie while satisfying the puzzle’s core rules.

D) Number/symbol placement in rows/columns/regions (Latin/arithmetic constraints)
- Latin-family with row/column/region constraints
  - Sudoku: Place digits so each row/column/box has 1–9 (plus any given variants).
  - Ripple Effect: Fill rooms with numbers; equal numbers in a row/column must be separated by that distance in cells.
  - Makaro: Place 1..n in rows/cols/rooms; in a cell, its arrow(s) must point to strictly larger neighbor(s) (inequality/neighbor ordering).
- Arithmetic crossword / equations
  - Nansuke: Fill a crossword-like grid with digits so across and down entries satisfy given arithmetic relationships (no word list; all numeric logic).
- Label relocation/permutation in rooms
  - Satogaeri: Move numbers along straight lines so each region ends up with the required set (often 1..k); paths don’t cross; moves obey distance/obstruction rules.

E) Vertex/edge graph connection (islands, bridges, networks)
- Hashiwokakero (Bridges): Connect numbered islands with 1–2 straight bridges so island degrees match numbers; no crossings; all islands connected.

F) Object placement and line-of-sight counting (not pure shading)
- Sto-stone: Place “stones” in cells; numbered circles count visible stones in orthogonal directions (or within a scope); adjacency/visibility rules restrict placements.
- Pencils: Place fixed-length pencil-shaped objects subject to row/column counts and non-touching/endpoint rules.
- Chained Block: Place/shade block runs to satisfy row/column clues while forming chained/linked block structures across the grid (run-based chaining constraints).

Notes
- Some titles are families with well-known variants; above, each is placed by its dominant mechanism.
- A few niche titles (e.g., Chained Block, Choco Banana, Juosan, Nagareru, Sto-stone, Pencils, Tilepaint) vary by source; the descriptions reflect common rulesets seen in logic-puzzle collections.
